document.title: Afghanistan's Key Players (U) - CIA leadership chart
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File (EBB 97) / Afghanistan 20/20
document.note: [Unclassified] One-page CIA chart of Afghanistan's factions and leaders circa 2001 (Taliban, Northern Alliance, Other Parties) with photos, comments and ethnicity. Transcribed from the image published by the National Security Archive (also reproduced as 3a.jpg in the 2021 'Afghanistan 20/20' briefing book). Transcription from image, not OCR.

persons.name: Mullah Mohammad Omar
persons.role: Leader and founder of the Taliban movement

mentions.quote: Leader and founder of movement... revered by followers... wants Islamic state with Sharia (Islamic law) enforced

persons.name: Mullah Mohammad Rabbani
persons.role: Second in command of the Taliban

mentions.quote: Second in command to Omar... more moderate... periodically sidelined by Omar

persons.name: Maulawi Wakil Mutawakil
persons.role: Taliban Foreign Minister; formerly the group's spokesperson

mentions.quote: Foreign Minister... close to Omar... relays Omar's views to outside world... formerly the group's spokesperson

persons.name: Mullah Abdul Jalil
persons.role: Taliban Deputy Foreign Minister; possible liaison with Bin Ladin

mentions.quote: Deputy Foreign Minister... close advisor to Omar... may serve as liaison with Bin Ladin.

persons.name: Usama Bin Ladin
persons.role: Guest in Afghanistan defended by Omar

mentions.quote: defends Usama Bin Ladin's stay in Afghanistan

persons.name: Ahmad Shah Masood
persons.role: Dominant military figure of the Northern Alliance (Jamiat-i-Islami)

mentions.quote: Dominant military figure in coalition... some ties to Iran, Russia... Panjsher Valley stronghold.

persons.name: Burhanuddin Rabbani
persons.role: Former nominal President of Afghanistan; Jamiat-i-Islami leader

mentions.quote: Former nominal President of Afghanistan... diminishing role and power in alliance
Currently in Iran... wary of Taliban's Shia policies... wants Shia role in future government.

persons.name: Ustad Mohaqqeq
persons.role: Major Shia commander, Hezbi Wahdat Akbari

mentions.quote: Major Shia commander... works nominally with Masood... well respected by his troops.
forced out of the country... currently moves between Iran and Turkey.

persons.name: Abdul Rasul Sayyaf
persons.role: Leader of Islamic Union for the Liberation of Afghanistan (IULA)
organizations: Islamic Union for the Liberation of Afghanistan

mentions.quote: Close to Masood... connected with terrorist training camps... ties to Saudis... anti-Shia

persons.name: Gulbuddin Hekmatyar
persons.role: Leader of Hezbi Islami-Gulbuddin; former Prime Minister

mentions.quote: Former Prime Minister... dislikes and mistrusts Masood... ties to Pakistan... currently in Iran.

persons.name: Mohammad Akbar Akbari
persons.role: Shia leader of Hezbi Wahdat Akbari

mentions.quote: Shia leader... wants guarantee of Shia rights, role in future government.

key_claims: Taliban controlled approximately 85% of Afghanistan by 2001 and fought a civil war with the Northern Alliance.
Omar defended Bin Ladin's stay in Afghanistan, while Mohammad Rabbani may have been at odds with Omar over him.
Mullah Abdul Jalil, Deputy Foreign Minister, may serve as liaison with Bin Ladin.
Sayyaf is linked to terrorist training camps and Saudi ties.
Masood is the dominant Northern Alliance military figure with Panjsher stronghold and ties to Iran and Russia.
Hekmatyar has ties to Pakistan and was in Iran.
